locator: VIII, lect. 9 n. 1040: if the first mover does not act, the last mover does not act
interpretation: Aquinas says Aristotle here proves the impossibility of an infinite series 'in a more certain way' than in Book VII: an infinite series has no first, and if the first mover does not act the last does not act, so there would be no mover, which is evidently false. Read as the same series principle as SCG I.13 [14]. Aquinas notes that the argument as such concludes no more that the first mover moves itself than that it is immobile. Basis: the English translation named in the passage manifest; a candidate for upgrade once a pinned Latin witness exists, and never a ground for overriding a reading of the Leonine/SCTA Latin.
